title: agent-debrief-gate: post-delegation completion debrief (forces a reflection lesson)
desc: The reframed agent-failure-reflection-gate (renamed 2026-07-17 failure->debrief): after a delegated subagent completes, if its mission outcome left no completion trace AND was not declared no-artifact-by-design, the harness blocks the next Agent dispatch until ROOT records a reflection lesson. It is a post-mission DEBRIEF, not a failure detector. Full dated incident history stays in the retained agent-failure-reflection-gate skill (the HQ catalog cannot yet delete/rename the old id -- core prune gap).
steps: WHAT IT IS: a DEBRIEF gate, not a failure detector. After a delegated agent (any tier/family via the native Agent tool) completes, on the NEXT dispatch the harness checks whether the previous agent's mission left a real completion trace (a commit, a passing test/parse-check, or a >=70-scored skill edit). If not -- and the dispatch was not declared no-artifact-by-design -- it blocks until ROOT records a reflection lesson on that model's reflection skill. The point is the post-mission debrief (capture the lesson), which is why 'debrief' replaced the misleading 'failure' framing.

CODE: the logic lives in the dot-sourced module tools/wkharness-guards-agent-debrief.ps1 (Get-WkAgentFailureGateVerdict + Test-WkRecentAgentFailure + the freshness check); the user-facing Block() with the [agent-debrief-gate] tag is emitted from the caller tools/wkharness-guards-agent.ps1. Internal function names still carry the AgentFailure prefix (intentionally kept during the rename to avoid churning 7 call sites).

THE NO-ARTIFACT-BY-DESIGN EXEMPTION (Test-WkDispatchDeclaredNoArtifact) -- VERIFIED WORKING 2026-07-17: a dispatch whose ORIGINAL ROOT prompt (read from the subagent transcript line-0, an un-fabricatable system-authored record) declares itself read-only/argument-only/measurement-only AND does not also request a fix/commit is EXEMPTED, so dialectic thesis/antithesis/synthesis and measurement probes are not false-flagged. Live-tested on real transcripts: argument-only dispatches return Exempt=True, IsFailure=False. Do NOT 'fix' this exemption on a hunch -- it works; measure before touching.

REFRAME PROVENANCE 2026-07-17 (user-directed): renamed because the 'failure' framing actively misled (ROOT nearly 'fixed' the working exemption because the name+prose read as broken). The CODE side (module file, dot-sources, guard tag, skill pointers) was renamed + live-verified this session (the gate fired under [agent-debrief-gate] = proof). The SKILL-side rename (this id + ~31 cross-references + HQ mirrors) is BLOCKED by a wkappbot-core gap: no skill rename subcommand, delete is an HQ no-op, sync has no prune-on-missing-source (filed as a suggest 2026-07-17). So this skill was CREATED fresh to coexist with the retained agent-failure-reflection-gate rather than renamed.

NAVIGATION: full dated incident history (the trace-less false-flag lineage, the line-0 exemption design, the freshness check) lives in the retained agent-failure-reflection-gate + agent-failure-reflection-gate-howto/-ref. The tool-family + core-gap that blocks the clean rename: wk-skill-reid-cleaner-spec. Twin gate: cheap-commit-todo-gate. Cross: delegation-completion-reflex-like-spec (the positive twin, pulse-on-success).

The repair patch is to parse shell_command/functions.shell_command arguments.command and then apply the same SkillId + --add-step + reward-window checks.

Correct fix order: first repair busy-fleet so built-in worker completion opens ROOT verification, then add Get-WkAgentDebriefReflectionSessionJsonl with WKHARNESS_TEST_REC_JSONL override first and cwd-matched newest Codex session fallback, then replace the verdict's sessJsonl selection and run Parser.ParseFile/diff-check/live Agent.cmd canary. Canary proof changed from stale haiku-reflection false block to a different proactive freshness block, proving this false-negative was cleared.

BUG 2026-07-23 score-source mismatch: wkappbot skill edit gpt-reflection reported knowledge-reward 100/100 after deleting fat incident steps, but the next Agent.cmd proactive freshness check still blocked with gpt-reflection score 61/100 below 70. Treat this as a scoring/catalog-path mismatch, not proof that the cleanup failed. Fix target: agent-debrief freshness must use the same SkillCoverageScore implementation and the same freshly synced project/HQ skill source that wkappbot skill edit rewards use, or print both source paths and scorer versions in the block message. Repro: delete a gpt-reflection fat step with wkappbot skill edit until reward says 100/100, then run Agent.cmd --model gpt-5-mini canary and compare the freshness score.

BUG 2026-07-23 Codex Agent.cmd collect-all regression: a single canary revealed blockers one at a time instead of one consolidated preflight report. Sequence observed: gpt-reflection freshness 59/61, then gemini-pro-reflection freshness 69, then harness-agent-brief-guard missing skill refs, then missing agent-on-load, then claude-md-diet-score 58, then CLAUDE.md repair-path blocks. This wastes user turns and tokens because each guard hides the next actionable blocker. Fix target: Agent.cmd/Codex preflight should collect proactive freshness, brief requirements, on-load requirement, diet score, and known repair-path blockers into one report before returning rc=2, or at least run the collect-all layer before first Block(). Repro: run Agent.cmd --model gpt-5-mini canary from wkappbot-kih after clearing one blocker at a time and compare sequential block messages.

LIVE REOPEN 2026-07-23 score-source mismatch blocks Codex delegation: wkappbot skill edit gpt-reflection --add-requirement printed knowledge-reward score 85/100 and stall reset, but the immediate Agent.cmd gate still reported gpt-reflection decayed to 63/100. This proves reward scoring and agent-debrief freshness scoring are reading different skill sources or stale caches. Fix direction: agent-debrief-gate must use the same canonical Get-WkSkillBaseScore/root set/cache invalidation as knowledge-reward, or include the source path/version in both messages.

ROOT CAUSE 2026-07-23 reflection freshness score mismatch: Get-WkAllReflectionSkillScores scans multiple skill roots but uses a seen set before scoring, so the first copy of gpt-reflection wins. If an older root copy scores 63 and a freshly edited root copy scores 85, Agent.cmd still blocks on 63. Fix: aggregate duplicate reflection ids across roots and keep the best/current score, or use one canonical root resolver shared with knowledge-reward.

[BUG][2026-07-23][codex-debrief-vs-stall-deadlock] When Agent.cmd is blocked by stale reflection-score aggregation, ROOT can also hit stall-guard before it can delegate the probe. Treat this as a harness repair deadlock: record the finding, then patch the score resolver directly with a minimal line-scoped edit and verify parser/diff before retrying Agent.cmd.

RESULT: SHIPPED 2026-07-23 -- now live in wkharness-guards-agent.ps1, the agent-debrief Block that fires when a delegated agent failed its mission (message text only; no logic touched; parses clean, harness -Status healthy). Original spec follows -- when a delegation comes back, the gate must demand TRUTH-VERIFICATION before acceptance, and on failure must send ROOT back to fix the BRIEF and re-dispatch until it passes. This is the twin of the busy-fleet second-delegation message (dispatch side); together they close the loop so the user does not have to say either half out loud. THE MESSAGE THE GATE SHOULD PRINT: 'Your agent is back. Before you believe a word of it: RE-RUN ITS COMMANDS YOURSELF and READ THE ARTIFACTS, not the summary. A report is intent; the file on disk is fact. Four false-pass shapes seen repeatedly in one session, all reported as fully green: (1) pasting the output of the RAW underlying CLI instead of the tool under test; (2) QUOTING THE SOURCE LINE (if not Prompt then exit 1) instead of running it; (3) answering a live criterion with framework active, ready to test; (4) a full checklist with no failing-half control -- and a test whose target would have passed anyway proves nothing. Also verify the BUILD ARTIFACT if it built: a wrong publish shape took this machine down for everyone while every command still looked normal. IF IT FAILED: do NOT swap models and do NOT do it yourself in frustration -- ITERATE THE BRIEF. Three failures in that session were each fixed by a sharper criterion, never by a different model. Sharpen with: a NONCE echoed before every command so a transcript cannot predate the brief; an EVIDENCE FILE at a path YOU name, so you read the artifact instead of the narrative; a demand for the FAILING HALF (show it not working without the change, then working with it); and the EXACT command named, wrapper included, so run the tool cannot degrade into run the thing the tool wraps. Then dispatch again. AND: an honest I could not do it, here is exactly where it broke IS a successful round -- rank it above a green checklist, say so to the agent, and keep that behaviour alive. FINALLY, THE COST ARGUMENT -- say it plainly, because it is the part everyone underestimates: claiming DONE without verifying is not a harmless shortcut, it is the MOST EXPENSIVE move available to you. A visible failure costs one round. An unverified success costs every round built on top of it, and you pay that bill later, in the dark, with interest. Measured in one session: a single log line that printed Injected N bytes over a discarded write result stood between us and the truth for hours, and THREE confident root-cause diagnoses were built on it before a checked write killed all three at once. Two other reports arrived fully green while the code did nothing at all. Nobody lied -- that is the point. Honest confidence is exactly what this gate exists to catch, which is why the currency here is EVIDENCE and not assurance. So never argue that it works; SHOW THE LINE THE MECHANISM PRINTS ABOUT ITSELF. If you cannot produce that line, you do not yet know, and saying so costs the least of all.' WIRING NOTE: the live text belongs in the debrief-gate implementation under D:/GitHub/wkappbot-kih/tools/; this step is the spec -- update both together or the guard will print advice its own skill no longer holds. See also: haiku-reflection-howto (the four briefing levers), delegation-verify-scorecard, verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static.

BUG: a still-running subagent permanently blocks every further dispatch through this gate. WHEN: you dispatched a background agent that is still working, and the next Agent call is refused no matter how many reflections you record. HOW: wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto -- then measure rather than guess: dot-source wkharness-common-nudge.ps1 and wkharness-guards-agent-debrief.ps1, call Get-WkAgentFailureGateVerdict twice a minute apart, and if Timestamp advances between the two calls this is the bug. WHY: measured live 2026-09-06 -- Get-WkNewestAgentFailureJsonl and Get-WkRecentAgentFailureJsonls choose candidates by LastWriteTime alone, so a running agent, writing its transcript continuously, is always the newest file. It carries no completion trace because it has not completed, so it reads as an ambiguous failure, and Test-WkRecentReflectionEdit demands a reflection edit later than that timestamp, which keeps moving. Observed 07:56:40Z then 07:57:49Z while the running transcript had been written 2 seconds earlier. Fix direction: judge only terminated transcripts, requiring a terminal result marker or excluding candidates written in the last 30 seconds, because an unfinished mission is not a failed one.
